title: Directed Clinical Practice I
description: This course is the beginning clinical experience of electroencephalographic (EEG) testing on patients at an affiliated neurodiagnostic laboratory. The clinical experience provides students a supervised application of previously-learned techniques and skills. These include application of electrodes, performance of EEG testing on clinical patients, medical recordkeeping and clinical history reporting in a timely manner. The focus is on safe, legal and professional behavior. This course also fosters the development of communication skills and interpersonal relationships required for the healthcare field. Supervision of the students is provided by a neurodiagnostic technologist and/or physician of the affiliating institution and is coordinated by the college faculty. This course is designed for students enrolled in the Neurodiagnostic Technology Program.
outcomes: Students will be able to apply electrodes accurately within 35 minutes and get the patient's test performed in an acceptable time
Student will be able to identify and monitor artifacts with 75% accuracy and identify normal EEG activity with 90% accuracy.
Accurately document all work, including calibrations, instrument settings, clinical findings, modifications to recording, and appropriate patient information.
objectives: Demonstrate professional behavior including willingness to adhere to policies, appropriate dress code, and absence/tardiness reporting guidelines.
Conduct self in an appropriate ethical manner as a health care professional including maintaining patient confidentiality and safety at all times.
Seek instruction and use feedback to improve performance.
Demonstrate a positive attitude to the clinical experience including making clinical performance a priority in their education.
Relate to patients in a positive manner to encourage patient cooperation and enhance attitude including good communication skills in explaining all procedures and expectations of the patient.
Maintain work area in an orderly manner, including obtaining and replacing supplies as needed and keeping work areas neat and clean.

Calibrate the machine with 100% accuracy and ability to make all necessary adjustments to the instrument for accurate recordings, including the proper use of cal voltage related to sensitivities and calibrating all settings used during a test.
Gather relevant and valid patient data.
Apply electrodes accurately within 35 minutes and get the patient's test performed in an acceptable time as per the lab schedule.
Use appropriate machine settings to provide optimal recording as necessary.
Identify and monitor artifacts with 75% accuracy.
Identify normal EEG activity with 90% accuracy.
Recognize abnormal events such as slow waves, spike &/or sharp activity, and other common discharges to approximately 50%.
Accurately document all work, including calibrations, instrument settings, clinical findings, modifications to recording, and appropriate patient information.
content: Regard for safety of others and self (including proper body mechanics)
Arrival at clinic on time and completing scheduled day, including accurate timecard reporting
Notification to college and clinic of expected tardiness and/or absence
Use of feedback to improve performance
Positive patient communication including appropriate explanation of procedures and expectations of patient
Maintenance of work area in orderly manner
Application of electrodes in timely and accurate manner
Appropriate machine settings for optimal recording
Ability to write description of each EEG performed
assignments: Professional journals including Journal of Clinical Neurophysiology and Neurodiagnostic Journal
Documentation of all work, including calibrations, instrument settings, clinical findings, modifications to recording, and appropriate patient information
Distinguishing between appropriate and inappropriate application principles of EEG.
Recognizing normal and basic abnormal EEG activity.
Reporting patient's clinical history, test results, and testing parameters.
